open_points.subject: A05 phase 7 cycle check
open_points.text: "cycles: the graph of nodes and edges is acyclic;"
open_points.question: Exactly which vertices are in the cycle graph for this check (only flow nodes, or flow inputs/outputs as well), and are guard relations part of it?
options: Cycle check over function/operation nodes only, using data edges between nodes
Cycle check over nodes plus flow input/output endpoints
Cycle check also includes guard-port dependencies as edges
open_points.default_guess: Cycle check over function/operation nodes only, using directed data edges between nodes.

open_points.subject: A05 phase 9 reach check
open_points.text: "reach: at least one output of every function node reaches, through edges and nodes, a flow output or an operation node..."
open_points.question: Does "reaches" mean structural reachability regardless of whether guard conditions are actually satisfiable at runtime, or only potentially deliverable paths?
options: Pure structural reachability (ignore runtime guard satisfiability)
Only paths that can actually deliver under at least one guard outcome

open_points.subject: A08 rule 5 manifest mismatch validation
open_points.text: "A proposal is refused as a manifest mismatch... when: the service record is absent, is not valid JSON, lacks `service` or `capabilities`..."
open_points.question: For malformed but present manifest structures (wrong JSON types, malformed capability items, missing nested fields used later), what exact failure detail and check order apply?
options: Treat any type/shape mismatch as the earliest listed check that needs that field and fail there
Introduce additional explicit sub-checks and reasons for each malformed shape
open_points.default_guess: Fail at the earliest listed check whose required field/type cannot be read, using that check’s mismatch reason.

open_points.subject: A17 service credentials presence vs runtime behavior
open_points.text: "the configuration file holds... per service, the selected manifest instance name and one credential" + "the instance... or its credential cannot be resolved... concludes `operation_failed`"
open_points.question: If a selected service has no configured credential reference at all (not just resolution failure), is startup refused, or does each send fail at runtime as `operation_failed`?
options: Refuse kernel startup when selected-service credential config is missing
Allow startup; fail per-send with pre-send `operation_failed` detail
open_points.default_guess: Refuse startup for missing credential configuration of a selected service.
